1.title: The Preacher Introduces Himself
1.text: Qoheleth (the 'Preacher' in Hebrew) reveals his position as 'son of David, king in Jerusalem' and begins his reflection on vanity.

1.question: According to the Preacher in chapter 1, what is the state of all things?
options: All things are permanent and lasting
Vanity of vanities
Everything is wise and comprehensible
All things are just and equitable

1.question: What does the Preacher say about renewal in the world?
options: All things are new each day
There is always something new under the sun
There is nothing new; all repeats
God creates new things continually

1.question: What conclusion does the Preacher reach after observing 'all that is done under the sun'?
options: It is all profit and lasting reward
It is all wisdom and eternal knowledge
It is vanity and vexation of spirit
It is all joy without any sorrow

1.question: What does the Preacher say about wisdom?
options: Increased wisdom increases happiness
In much wisdom is much grief
Wisdom never brings suffering
Only fools suffer; the wise do not

2.title: The Preacher Seeks Pleasures
2.text: He decided to try laughter, joy, wine, and sensory pleasures to see if life has value.

2.question: How did the Preacher build and accumulate possessions?
options: He built great temples, palaces, and fortresses
He bought many servants, flocks, and vast lands
He made pools of water, orchards, and gardens
He received gold and silver from the royal treasury

2.question: After accumulating all he desired, what was the Preacher's conclusion?
options: He attained complete happiness
He saw it was great deception
He discovered it was all vanity
He became completely satisfied

2.question: What is the difference between the wise and the fool according to the Preacher?
options: The wise hides his wisdom, while the fool reveals it to all
The wise has light in his eyes; the fool walks in darkness
The wise seeks riches, the fool seeks only fleeting pleasures
The wise lives a long life, the fool dies young

2.question: What does the Preacher question about his labors?
options: They will surely be multiplied and preserved forevermore
They bring no value beyond the present moment at all times
Who knows if he will be wise or a fool to inherit all
They will remain with him forever guaranteed

2.question: To whom does God grant wisdom and knowledge according to the Preacher?
options: To everyone who seeks earthly riches
To the priests chosen in the sacred temple
To a man who is good in His sight
To the wisest elders of the city

3.title: A Time for Everything
3.text: The Preacher presents the idea that everything has its appointed time: birth, death, planting, harvest, war, and peace.

3.question: Complete: 'A time to seek, and a time to ___'
options: find
lose
keep
choose

3.question: What is the work that God has given to men?
options: To rest peacefully and grow rich always
To occupy themselves and be afflicted
To govern kingdoms and conquer distant lands
To seek only pleasure and comfort

3.question: What has God put in men's hearts?
options: The desire for riches
Eternity
Fear of death
The will to dominate

3.question: What conclusion does the Preacher draw about the best thing for man?
options: To accumulate power and riches forever
To rejoice and enjoy his labor
To conquer death and live forever always
To become king of all the earth

4.title: Oppression in the World
4.text: The Preacher observes the oppressed without a comforter, seeing that there is vanity in all labor that man does.

4.question: What is better according to the Preacher?
options: The fool always works too hard without ever resting
Only to rest without ever working at all times
A handful with quiet than both hands with toil
To work without ever stopping for real

4.question: What advantage has a companion according to the Preacher?
options: There is no real advantage in having one
If one falls, the other will lift him up
It doubles his wealth forever without end
It avoids all forms of death entirely

4.question: What does the Preacher observe about the new king who ascends to the throne?
options: He is praised eternally by all the surrounding peoples
There is no end at all to his fame nor his popularity
Those who come after will not rejoice in him
He reigns guaranteed for a hundred long years

5.title: Warning Against Rash Vows
5.text: The Preacher warns against making rash and easy vows to God; it is better not to vow than to vow and not fulfill.

5.question: What is better according to the Preacher?
options: To make rash vows
To guard your mouth
To speak much to God
To promise everything you desire

5.question: What truth does the Preacher affirm about he who loves money?
options: He is easily satisfied
He is never satisfied
He can rest easy
He lives a happy life

5.question: What happens when wealth is lost?
options: It always returns to its original owner
It brings absolutely no suffering at all
It generates frustration and pain
It is quickly replaced soon after

5.question: How should the laborer's life be according to the Preacher?
options: To always think of distant future ambitions
To enjoy his labor; this is a gift from God
To accumulate as much wealth as possible always
To reject every pleasure of this life

6.title: A Great Evil
6.text: The Preacher observes the man to whom God gave wealth but does not let him enjoy it; another enjoys it in his place.

6.question: According to the Preacher, which life is better?
options: To live a thousand years twice without ever resting fully
A stillborn is better than to live long in vanity
To have extreme longevity accompanied by great wealth
To live an entire life in complete poverty

6.question: What does the Preacher not know?
options: His own true name among all the surrounding peoples
Who God truly is and exactly where he dwells
What is good for man; what will be after him
Exactly where he will die someday far away

7.title: In Praise of Wisdom
7.text: The Preacher begins to exalt wisdom, recognizing that no one can be successful without it.

7.question: What is better according to the Preacher?
options: The joy of the house of banquet
The brief anger of the wise
The constant laughter of the fool
Calmness without limits

7.question: What is the benefit of wisdom and money?
options: Only money grants protection, but it does not prolong the owner's life
Only wisdom truly protects; money serves no real purpose at all
Both protect, but wisdom preserves the life of its possessors
Neither wisdom nor money brings any real benefit to man

7.question: What advice does the Preacher give?
options: Be extremely just in everything that you do
Be neither too just nor too ungodly
Practice evil without any restriction or limit
Always seek total perfection

7.question: What truth does the Preacher state about men?
options: Every man who fears God lives without ever committing sin
There is not a just man who does good and never sins
There are many just men who never do any wickedness at all
The wise man never makes any mistake before God

7.question: What did the Preacher find about men and women?
options: All men and women alike are equally upright and virtuous
One upright man among a thousand and no upright woman
No man or woman ever fully attains true righteousness
Women are more righteous than men in every land

8.title: Wisdom Illuminates
8.text: A man's wisdom illuminates his face, changing his severity. The Preacher reflects on obedience to the king.

8.question: According to the Preacher, who will resist the king?
options: Anyone
No one
Only the wise
Kings of other nations

8.question: What truth does the Preacher affirm?
options: No one has power over the wind
Everyone has power over destiny
Man controls death
Life is completely predictable

8.question: What will be the fate of the wicked?
options: He will live many years in great prosperity
His days will be prolonged as a shadow
His days will be good and full of blessings
He will suffer no punishment for his deeds

8.question: What conclusion does the Preacher reach?
options: The wise fully comprehends all the work that God performs under the sun
Though the wise thinks to know, he cannot comprehend God's work
Man can fully grasp and understand all of God's designs and purposes
God will reveal all his plans to those who seek with faith

9.title: Death Comes to All
9.text: Death comes to the just and unjust, the clean and unclean, to the sacrificer and to those who do not sacrifice.

9.question: What does the Preacher affirm about the dead?
options: They still know everything that happens among the living
They know nothing more; their memory is forgotten
They live in another realm awaiting the day of final judgment
They can still judge the actions of the living

9.question: What advice does the Preacher give?
options: Work only when you feel like it and never hurry in any way
Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with all your might
Do nothing important, for everything is vanity and meaningless
Let others do all the hard work while you simply rest

9.question: What illustration does the Preacher use about wisdom?
options: Little wisdom preserves a great city
Wisdom is completely useless against great walls
Rich and powerful cities never need any wisdom
Wisdom never helps save a city

9.question: What does the folly of a single fool do?
options: It affects nothing in the city or its people
It destroys much wisdom and honor
It increases the glory and honor of the city
It protects the whole entire city

10.title: Dead Flies and Folly
10.text: Dead flies cause the perfumer's ointment to putrefy. A little folly ruins much wisdom.

10.question: How should one behave when facing someone who is furious?
options: Confront his anger immediately with harsh and firm words to restrain his fury
If the spirit of the ruler rises against you, do not abandon your place
Flee immediately and with great fear from the place before his anger turns on you
Always openly defy the authority of the one who rules over you

10.question: What danger is there in risky activities?
options: No real danger truly exists at all
He who digs a pit falls into it
Everyone comes out completely unscathed
The axe never becomes dull

10.question: What does the fool constantly do?
options: Always speaks with great wisdom on every occasion
Multiplies words about things he does not know
Keeps complete silence in the presence of everyone
Only listens carefully to what others say

10.question: According to the Preacher, what should we not even do?
options: Rest completely without ever working again
Work excessively until all strength is gone
Even in thought curse the king
Study the scriptures very deeply

11.title: Cast Your Bread Upon the Waters
11.text: The Preacher encourages generosity: cast your bread upon the waters and after many days you will find it.

11.question: Why should we be generous according to the Preacher?
options: We will always know when we will prosper
We do not know what misfortune may come
Only the rich should be generous
Generosity never helps

11.question: What advice does the Preacher give to young people?
options: Suffer with deep sorrow all the days of your life
Rejoice in your youth; light is sweet
Focus only on work and forget all joy
Reject every form of pleasure in youth

12.title: Remember Your Creator
12.text: In youth, remember your Creator. The body ages and death approaches; all is vanity.

12.question: How does the Preacher describe the aging process?
options: The body grows stronger and the mind becomes clearer with age
The silver cord loosens, the golden bowl breaks
The eyes become sharper and the arms grow stronger with age
Youth fully returns and strength is renewed

12.question: What did the Preacher seek?
options: Pleasing words and honest truths
Riches and pleasures for all the people
Fame and power among the wise of the land
Worldly glory and honor for himself

12.question: What is the final conclusion of the book?
options: Seeking riches and pleasures is the only true purpose of human life
Fear God and keep His commandments; this is the whole duty of man
Human wisdom alone is enough to attain full and lasting happiness
There is no final judgment; each one lives and dies as he chooses
